messages.subject: Identical elite configurations
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am running irace for an algorithm with three input variables (i.e., gamma, x and y). The domain for these variables are currently as follows:

# name   switch      type   values
  gamma  "--gamma "  c      (1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
  y      "--y "      c      (10, 20 ,30)
  x         "--x "      c            (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12)

Ironically, irace reports identical elite configurations (please look at the photo below for further information). I was wondering what could be the reason for this issue. Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: Identical elite configurations
messages.body_plain:
This is a known problem with the current version of irace and it is in the (very long) TODO list of potential improvements.

Currently, irace does not check for duplicated configurations because it is too time-consuming and many benchmarks measure the CPU-time of irace, so slowing irace down is not an option. When the configuration space is large, duplicates are extremely rare so checking for them is a waste of time. I have several ideas on how to check and handle such duplicates without slowing down irace, but they require changing the code of irace substantially.

The issue is more visible in your scenario because you have a very small configuration space (90 configurations only). In that case, irace may find a good configuration multiple times and, since there is no detection of duplicates, they will be reported as elite because they perform similarly. With such small configuration space, it would make more sense to test all configurations using one race (not an iterated racing procedure). Of course, it is not 100% obvious when is it better to use irace and when it is better to use a single race. This is an open research question as far as I know. Ideally, irace would detect such a case and do the right thing, but this requires additional development work.

If you (or anyone) would like to collaborate with me in testing and implementing these ideas, please write to my email: manuel.lo...@uma.es

The next version of irace (version 3.5) already implements an idea to alleviate this issue  but it does not eliminate it completely. You can install version 3.5 from Github: https://github.com/MLopez-Ibanez/irace#github-development-version and report back whether it helps. Version 3.5 should become the next stable version before the summer (we would like to do a bit more testing before publishing it in CRAN).

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Irace Team, I am trying to run an algorithm with parallelism in irace and it works very well, however when enabling parallelism in Irace the algorithm begins to crash

scenario <- list(targetRunner = target.runner,
                           trainInstancesDir = path("ds","dset"),
                           digits = 2,
                           maxExperiments = 300,
                           parallel = 4,
                           logFile = "irace.Rdata")

checkIraceScenario(scenario, parameters = parameters)

# Warning occurred when running targetRunner:
1 function calls resulted in an error
Error in socketConnection("localhost", port = port, server = TRUE, blocking = TRUE, : can't open connection
# An error occurred while running targetRunner:
== irace == A child process triggered a fatal error
# targetRunner returned:
NULL
Error: == irace == Check failed.

tuned.confs <- irace(scenario = scenario, parameters = parameters)

Error in socketConnection("localhost", port = port, server = TRUE, lock = TRUE, :
can not open the connection
Error: == irace == A child process triggered a fatal error
In addition: Warning message:
In parallel::mclapply(experiments, exec.target.runner, mc.preschedule = !scenario$loadBalancing, :
7 function calls resulted in an error

it can be fixed?

Regards
JAC
